core: It marks that the subject received an action, usually something unwanted or unexpected. Many learners overuse it for neutral actions — most everyday passive events in Chinese use 让/叫/给 instead.

collocations.en: to have been taken by someone

sentences.pinyin: wǒ de shǒujī bèi tōu le.
sentences.why: You tell your roommate the moment you realize your phone is gone. 被 here frames the theft as something that happened to you against your will.
sentences.tip: Stress 偷 slightly; this is the most natural way to say something was stolen.

sentences.situation: Office break room · to a colleague
sentences.zh: 我今天早上被老板骂了。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ jīntiān zǎoshang bèi lǎobǎn mà le.
sentences.en: I got scolded by the boss this morning.
sentences.why: A colleague complains about being reprimanded. 被 marks the scolding as an unpleasant experience received from the boss.
sentences.tip: If you don't name the person, say 被骂了一顿.

sentences.situation: On the phone · to your spouse
sentences.zh: 我的自行车被人骑走了。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ de zìxíngchē bèi rén qí zǒu le.
sentences.why: You call home after finding your bike missing. 被人 makes it clear an unknown person took it.
sentences.tip: Native speakers often say 被人拿走了 for smaller items.

sentences.zh: 我的饭卡被同学借走了。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ de fànkǎ bèi tóngxué jiè zǒu le.
sentences.en: My meal card was borrowed by a classmate.
sentences.why: You explain why you can't buy lunch. 被 here is neutral-sounding because the borrowing was probably legitimate, but you still suffered the inconvenience.
sentences.tip: Don't say 被偷 if you know who took it.

sentences.zh: 这个项目被推迟到下个月了。
sentences.pinyin: zhège xiàngmù bèi tuīchí dào xià gè yuè le.
sentences.en: This project was pushed to next month.
sentences.why: You report a schedule change. 被 frames the delay as a decision made by higher-ups, not by you.
sentences.tip: In formal emails, 被推迟 is common; in speech, 推迟到了 also works.

sentences.zh: 我的报告被王经理退回了。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ de bàogào bèi Wáng jīnglǐ tuìhuí le.
sentences.en: My report was sent back by Manager Wang.
sentences.why: You message your manager to explain a setback. 被退回 is the standard office term for a document being rejected.
sentences.tip: Avoid complaining about Wang here; just state the fact.

sentences.situation: At a meeting · to your team
sentences.zh: 他被选为我们的新组长。
sentences.pinyin: tā bèi xuǎnwéi wǒmen de xīn zǔzhǎng.
sentences.en: He was chosen as our new team leader.
sentences.why: You announce an appointment. 被选为 is the fixed formal phrase for being elected or selected.
sentences.tip: This is one of the few neutral uses of 被; it's always used for selections.

sentences.zh: 我之前被公司派到上海工作过两年。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ zhīqián bèi gōngsī pài dào Shànghǎi gōngzuò guo liǎng nián.
sentences.en: I was sent by my company to work in Shanghai for two years.
sentences.why: You describe past experience. 被派 frames the assignment as a company decision, showing you followed orders.
sentences.tip: Stress 派 to sound confident; don't say 我自己去上海.

sentences.zh: 他因为迟到太多被公司开除了。
sentences.pinyin: tā yīnwèi chídào tài duō bèi gōngsī kāichú le.
sentences.en: He was fired by the company for being late too many times.
sentences.why: This sentence appears in official announcements. 被开除 is the formal term for termination.
sentences.tip: In casual speech, people say 被炒鱿鱼 instead.

sentences.pinyin: bié nánguò, nǐ méiyǒu bèi wàngjì.
sentences.en: Don't be sad, you haven't been forgotten.
sentences.why: You comfort a friend who feels left out. 被忘记 is a softer, emotional use of the passive.
sentences.tip: Say this gently; stress 没有.

quiz.prompt: Tell your friend that your wallet was stolen on the subway.
quiz.answer: 我的钱包在地铁上被偷了。
quiz.explain: 被偷 is the standard phrase for theft, and adding 在地铁上 gives the location naturally.

quiz.prompt: Explain to your classmate that your textbook was borrowed by another student.
quiz.answer: 我的课本被同学借走了。
quiz.explain: 被借走 shows the item was taken by someone else, causing you inconvenience.

quiz.prompt: You are telling your manager that your proposal was rejected by the client, in a polite, professional tone.
quiz.answer: 我们的方案被客户退回了。
accept: 我们的方案被客户拒绝了。
quiz.explain: 被退回 or 被拒绝 is the standard office phrasing for a proposal being turned down.

quiz.prompt: Comfort your friend who feels left out of the group chat, using 被 in a warm way.
accept: 大家没有忘记你，别难过。
quiz.explain: 被忘记 is a soft, emotional passive that reassures someone they are still cared about.

quiz.prompt: 你的自行车怎么不见了？
quiz.answer: 我的自行车被人骑走了。
quiz.explain: When asked why your bike is gone, 被人骑走 naturally explains an unknown person took it.

quiz.prompt: 你昨天为什么没去开会？
quiz.answer: 我被老板叫去办公室了。
quiz.explain: 被叫走 explains you were pulled away by someone else, which is the common reason for missing a meeting.
